## Hypothesis

H1: The perceived morality of infidelity (IV) will effect willingness to marry without love (DV).

H2: Sex (categorical IV) will affect time spent dressing well (DV).


## Load the processed data

```{r loadData}
#load processed data
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)
install.packages("ggrain")

h1Data <- read.csv("/Users/srb/R Studio/PSY 221A/PSY221A-HW/data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("/Users/srb/R Studio/PSY 221A//PSY221A-HW/data/processed_data/h2.csv")
#reorganize categorical variable
table(h2Data$Sex_birth)
h2Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h2Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

```

## H2 - Box Plot

```{r H2Box}
#Box plot
#The line is the median; the box covers the middle 50% of responses (Q1-Q3).
#Whiskers reach the most extreme observations within 1.5 IQR of the box edges.
h2Box <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=Time_A_dress_1,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_boxplot () +
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
        y="Amount of time spent on dressing well",
        title="Time spent dressing well by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=8) #changes font size

h2Box
```

## H1 - Violin Plot (with Box Plot)

```{r H1Violin}
#Violin Plot
#Wider sections show where responses are more concentrated within each group.
#The shape depends on smoothing; integer scores can create bumps.

# The perceived morality of infidelity (IV) will effect willingness to marry without love (DV).

###JK: Match the H1 column names to your CSV and use a scatterplot for these two numeric scores. ###
# Both H1 variables are continuous, so a scatterplot is a better choice for showing their relationship than a violin or raincloud plot.
# The example below creates a jittered scatterplot with a trend line. I changed the name h1Rain to h1Point so you'll have to change the save code to use this name.
# read.csv() imports your columns as Perceived.morality and Willingness.to.marry, instead of moral, willing_marry.
# For H1, replace the violin and raincloud blocks with this example and keep the name h1Rain so your save code still works:
# h1Point <- ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Perceived.morality, y = Willingness.to.marry)) +
#   geom_jitter(width = .1, height = 0, alpha = .1) +
#   geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
#   labs(x = "Perceived moral wrongness of infidelity", y = "Willingness to marry without love") +
#   theme_minimal()
###  End of comment ###

h1Viol <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=moral,
                    y=willing_marry,
                    fill=moral))+
  labs(x="Morality of Infidelity",
        y="Willingness to Marry without Love",
        title="Inherent Morality of Infidelity's influence on Willingness to marry without love")+
  theme_gray(base_size=8)+
  geom_violin()+ #order doesn't usually matter
  geom_boxplot(width=.12)


h1Viol
```

## H1 - Raincloud Plot

```{r H1Raincloud}
#Raincloud Plot
#A raincloud combines a half-violin, a box plot, and individual responses.

# The perceived morality of infidelity (IV) will effect willingness to marry without love (DV).
h1Rain <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=moral,
                    y=willingness_marry,
                    fill=moral))+
  labs(x="Morality of Infidelity",
        y="Willingness to Marry without Love",
        title="Inherent Morality of Infidelity's influence on Willingness to marry without love",
       fill="Morality of Infidelity")+
  geom_rain(alpha=.5)+
  theme(minimal(base_size))

h1Rain
```
